points.place: 肯塔基州哈丁县（今拉鲁县）
points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 林肯出生于肯塔基州一个贫困的拓荒家庭，父母是托马斯·林肯和南希·汉克斯。童年时期，林肯接受了有限的正规教育，主要依靠自学。9岁时母亲去世，继母莎拉·布什·约翰逊对他影响深远。这段时期，林肯培养了强烈的阅读习惯和对知识的渴望，同时形成了对奴隶制的初步认识，这些经历深刻影响了他后来的政治立场和价值观。1830年，林肯随家人迁往伊利诺伊州，开始了新的人生阶段。
points.descriptionEn: Lincoln was born in a poor frontier family in Kentucky to Thomas Lincoln and Nancy Hanks. He received limited formal education and was largely self-taught. His mother died when he was nine, and his stepmother, Sarah Bush Johnston, had a profound influence on him. During this period, Lincoln developed a strong reading habit and thirst for knowledge while forming his initial views on slavery. In 1830, he moved with his family to Illinois, marking a new phase in his life.

points.place: 伊利诺伊州新塞勒姆和斯普林菲尔德
points.title: 法律与政治起步
points.description: 林肯在伊利诺伊州开始了他的法律和政治生涯。他担任过多种工作，包括测量员、店员和邮局局长。1834年，林肯首次当选伊利诺伊州议员，开始了长达八年的政治生涯。在此期间，他成为辉格党的重要成员，支持银行、内部改进和工业发展。1837年，林肯在斯普林菲尔德开设律师事务所，与威廉·亨登合作。1842年，他与玛丽·托德结婚。这一时期，林肯逐渐确立了自己的政治立场，反对奴隶制扩张，但尚未主张立即废除奴隶制。1846年，林肯当选美国众议员，在华盛顿度过了两年时光。
points.descriptionEn: Lincoln began his legal and political career in Illinois. He worked as a surveyor, store clerk, and postmaster. In 1834, he was first elected to the Illinois General Assembly, starting an eight-year political career. During this time, he became an important member of the Whig Party, supporting banks, internal improvements, and industrial development. In 1837, he opened a law practice in Springfield with William Herndon. In 1842, he married Mary Todd. This period saw Lincoln establish his political stance against the expansion of slavery, though not yet advocating for immediate abolition. In 1846, he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, serving in Washington for two years.

points.place: 伊利诺伊州斯普林菲尔德
points.title: 重返政坛与废奴运动
points.description: 在短暂的退休后，林肯因堪萨斯-内布拉斯加法案（1854年）而重返政坛，该法案允许新领土的居民自行决定是否允许奴隶制。林肯加入新成立的共和党，成为反对奴隶制扩张的领导者。1858年，他与斯蒂芬·道格拉斯进行了著名的林肯-道格拉斯辩论，就奴隶制问题展开激烈交锋。尽管最终未能当选参议员，这些辩论使林肯在全国范围内获得了知名度。他发表了著名的《家庭分裂》演讲，警告奴隶制问题可能导致国家分裂。这一时期，林肯的政治思想逐渐成熟，从反对奴隶制扩张转向反对奴隶制本身，为1860年总统大选奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: After a brief retirement, Lincoln returned to politics due to the Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854), which allowed territories to decide on slavery through popular sovereignty. Lincoln joined the newly formed Republican Party and became a leader against the expansion of slavery. In 1858, he engaged in the famous Lincoln-Douglas Debates with Stephen Douglas, having intense exchanges on the slavery issue. Though he lost the Senate race, these debates brought him national recognition. He delivered his famous 'House Divided' speech, warning that the slavery issue could lead to national division. During this period, Lincoln's political thinking matured, shifting from opposing slavery expansion to opposing slavery itself, laying the groundwork for his 1860 presidential campaign.

points.title: 总统任期与内战
points.description: 1861年3月4日，林肯就任美国第16任总统。不久后，南方各州宣布脱离联邦，美国内战爆发。林肯面临维护国家统一的巨大挑战。他采取了一系列关键措施：任命有能力的军事将领（最终找到格兰特）、颁布《解放黑人奴隶宣言》（1863年）、推动通过《宅地法》和《太平洋铁路法案》。林肯还发表了著名的葛底斯堡演说（1863年），重新定义了美国的民主理念。在战争期间，林肯面临政治反对、个人悲痛（爱子威廉去世）以及战争带来的巨大压力。1864年，林肯成功连任，继续领导国家走向胜利。1865年4月14日，林肯在福特剧院被约翰·威尔克斯·布斯刺杀，成为美国第一位被刺杀的总统。
points.descriptionEn: On March 4, 1861, Lincoln was inaugurated as the 16th President of the United States. Shortly after, Southern states seceded from the Union, and the American Civil War began. Lincoln faced the immense challenge of preserving the Union. He implemented several key measures: appointing capable military leaders (eventually finding Grant), issuing the Emancipation Proclamation (1863), and promoting the Homestead Act and Pacific Railway Act. Lincoln also delivered the famous Gettysburg Address (1863), redefining American democratic ideals. During the war, he faced political opposition, personal grief (the death of his son Willie), and the immense pressure of war. In 1864, Lincoln was re-elected and continued to lead the nation toward victory. On April 14, 1865, Lincoln was assassinated by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre, becoming the first U.S. president to be assassinated.

points.place: 伊利诺伊州斯普林菲尔德
points.title: 身后影响
points.description: 林肯遇刺后被运回斯普林菲尔德安葬。他的去世震惊了全国，但也加速了重建进程。林肯的政治遗产包括维护国家统一、废除奴隶制、加强联邦政府权力以及推动经济发展。他的领导风格、道德勇气和演讲才能使他成为美国历史上最受尊敬的总统之一。林肯的思想影响了后来的民权运动，他的形象被用于各种政治和社会运动中。在斯普林菲尔德，林肯故居、墓地和总统图书馆成为重要的历史遗址，每年吸引大量游客。林肯的形象也出现在美国货币（5美元纸币和1美分硬币）和纪念性建筑（林肯纪念堂）上，成为美国民主和自由的象征。
points.descriptionEn: After his assassination, Lincoln's body was transported to Springfield for burial. His death shocked the nation but also accelerated the Reconstruction process. Lincoln's political legacy includes preserving the Union, abolishing slavery, strengthening federal government power, and promoting economic development. His leadership style, moral courage, oratory skills have made him one of the most revered presidents in American history. Lincoln's ideas influenced later civil rights movements, and his image has been used in various political and social causes. In Springfield, his home, tomb, and presidential library serve as important historical sites attracting numerous visitors annually. Lincoln's image appears on U.S. currency (the $5 bill and 1-cent coin) and in memorial buildings (the Lincoln Memorial), symbolizing American democracy and freedom.

supporter.zh: 林肯被赞誉为美国最伟大的总统之一，他领导国家度过了最严重的分裂危机，维护了国家统一，并废除了奴隶制，为美国的民主和自由奠定了基础。他的领导风格体现了坚定的原则性与灵活的策略性相结合，特别是在内战期间展现出的非凡毅力和道德勇气。林肯的《解放黑人奴隶宣言》和葛底斯堡演说成为美国民主精神的经典表达，影响了后世无数追求平等和自由的斗争。他被视为民主制度的捍卫者和人权先驱，其政治遗产至今仍在塑造着美国的价值观。
supporter.en: Lincoln is celebrated as one of America's greatest presidents, leading the nation through its most severe crisis, preserving the Union, and abolishing slavery, thereby laying the foundation for American democracy and freedom. His leadership style combined steadfast principles with flexible strategies, demonstrating extraordinary perseverance and moral courage during the Civil War. Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation and Gettysburg Address have become classic expressions of American democratic spirit, influencing countless struggles for equality and freedom throughout history. He is regarded as a defender of democratic institutions and a pioneer of human rights, with his political legacy still shaping American values today.

critic.zh: 批评者指出林肯在内战期间采取的措施，包括暂停人身保护令、限制言论自由和军事征兵，构成了对宪法的侵犯。一些历史学家认为林肯对奴隶制的立场存在矛盾，早期主要关注限制奴隶制扩张而非立即废除。此外，有批评者认为林肯的重建计划过于宽容，未能有效保护被解放奴隶的权利，导致南方种族隔离制度的长期存在。还有人质疑林肯对印第安人的政策，特别是在达科他战争中的处理方式。这些批评者认为，尽管林肯的成就值得肯定，但其领导方式也存在专制倾向和对少数群体权益的忽视。
critic.en: Critics point out that Lincoln's actions during the Civil War, including suspending the writ of habeas corpus, restricting freedom of speech, and military conscription, constituted violations of the Constitution. Some historians argue that Lincoln's position on slavery was inconsistent, initially focusing on limiting its expansion rather than immediate abolition. Additionally, critics contend that Lincoln's Reconstruction plans were too lenient, failing to adequately protect the rights of freed slaves, leading to the long-term existence of Southern segregation. Others question Lincoln's policies toward Native Americans, particularly his handling of the Dakota War. These critics maintain that while Lincoln's achievements are noteworthy, his leadership style contained authoritarian tendencies and neglect of minority rights.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，林肯被复杂而多维地定义。历史学家普遍认可他在维护国家统一和废除奴隶制方面的历史贡献，同时也客观分析其政策的历史背景和局限性。林肯的形象已超越政治人物，成为美国民主、自由和种族平等的象征符号。在流行文化中，林肯经常被引用为道德领导力的典范，其生平故事被改编成电影、文学作品和艺术作品。然而，当代历史研究也呈现出更复杂的林肯形象，承认他在种族问题上的矛盾立场，以及其政策对印第安人和其他少数群体的影响。这种多维度评价反映了历史认知的演变和历史的复杂性。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Lincoln is defined in complex and multidimensional ways. Historians generally acknowledge his historical contributions to preserving the Union and abolishing slavery while objectively analyzing the historical context and limitations of his policies. Lincoln's image has transcended politics to become a symbolic representation of American democracy, freedom, and racial equality. In popular culture, Lincoln is frequently cited as a model of moral leadership, with his life story adapted into films, literary works, and art. However, contemporary historical research presents a more complex Lincoln, acknowledging his contradictory positions on racial issues and the impact of his policies on Native Americans and other minorities. This multidimensional evaluation reflects the evolution of historical understanding and the complexity of history itself.

self.zh: 民有、民治、民享的政府永世长存。
self.en: Government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.

others.zh: 林肯是美国历史上最伟大的道德领袖之一，他不仅改变了美国的政治进程，还重塑了美国人的道德想象。
others.en: Lincoln was one of the greatest moral leaders in American history, who not only changed the course of American politics but also reshaped the moral imagination of the American people.
